correctness.rationale: For weighted observations ±a, likelihood strict concavity in the two fitted kernel means gives uniqueness when the dual equality support is ≤2. Reconstructed sensitivity D_delta(z+t)=exp(-t²/2)[q exp(-2a(1-q)t)+(1-q)exp(2aqt)] with z=a(1-2q); published Schlemm sharp Kearns–Saul Bernoulli moment inequality, including its nonzero equality case, yields singleton iff a≤a_c(q). The derivative-stationarity equation for a positive Gaussian mixture has at most two local maxima, bounding any optimum support by two; linear independence of the two fitted kernel vectors proves unique measure. For unequal q, critical second dual contact at -z and negative curvature up to a_loc justify discontinuous-support onset with vanishing mass; q=1/2 contacts coalesce. Exact Gamma normalization gives Q~Beta(α,α), and a_c monotonic in |1−2q| yields 1−2I_{(1−x_a)/2}(α,α), with artanh(x_a)=a²x_a; x_a~sqrt(3(a²−1)). Independent numerical sensitivity and Beta checks confirm sample values but do not replace the global Kearns–Saul proof.
